gmText: Jax left a Crown courier loft above the Close behind and took the narrow back way through the morning, with wet stone underfoot and washing strung between the walls. Jax walked on alone toward Cathedral Close, saying nothing about the Earth kit still weighing down the old bag on their shoulder. Four thugs stepped out across the lane, and Col Tew stood in front with a loud, easy laugh that bounced off the shutters. "Easy there, friend. Small toll for the road, and you go on your way," Col Tew said, and held out one open hand. Behind Col Tew the other two waited, and one of them tapped a short wooden club against his own palm.

gmText: Cathedral Close was bright with morning light, and Jax stood in the courtyard where the kitchens sent out warm bread smells. Jax walked on across the flagstones, past a cart of turnips and two women sorting laundry into wicker baskets. Nell Rudd looked up from her basket, gave Jax a long, weighing look, and went back to her work without a word. Maud Thatch said, without turning around, "You are new here. That or you have come to see the Chanter." To the left, a narrow door under the west wall stood open and dark, and somewhere inside a bell rang once.

stageTrace.text: Jax kept their eyes on Maud Thatch and watched how the tired woman held her shoulders and how she glanced at the church doors. Maud Thatch let out a long breath and told Jax that the Chanter up at the Cathedral Close does not like questions from the likes of her. Maud Thatch stood with her arms folded, watching the big doors of the Cathedral Close across the gravel yard.
